**PotentialNoise 2.2.0**

- **GUIDE page**: the pink-noise method one tap per track. Pull your faders down and tap **NEXT**: the noise comes on and the guide names each part of your beat in turn (kick, snare / clap, bass, hi-hats, percussion, main sample / chords, melody / lead, vocals, pads / texture, FX), with what to listen for. Parts you don't have are one tap to skip, **BACK** goes back one, and the last tap switches the noise off. **DRUMS FIRST** or **SAMPLE FIRST** sets the order, and your project remembers it.
- Seven parameters were added at the end of the list for the page; saved projects open as before.

**Downloads**
- **`PotentialNoise-2.2.0-akai-vst2.zip`**: for **MPC OS 3.10.1 or later**, any standalone MPC (32-bit and 64-bit). Turn on **External Plugin Support** in Preferences → Enhancements (Beta), unzip, and copy the folder into **VST2 Plugins** at the top of a drive. See the [install guide](https://github.com/PotentialBreakfast/mpc-vst-potentialnoise/blob/main/INSTALL-GUIDE.md).
- **`PotentialNoise-2.2.0-mpc-sdk.zip`**: the same plugin folder in the Open MPC catalog's 3.10.1 format (one folder for every MPC).
- **`PotentialNoise-2.2.0-mpc-armv7.zip`**: for Gen1 MPCs with the community plugin set-up on older MPC OS 3.x. Install it with the [Open MPC](https://open-mpc.github.io/) installer app, or follow `INSTALL.md` inside the zip. Save your project first, because installing restarts the MPC.
- **`PotentialNoise-2.2.0-mpc-aarch64.zip`**: the same for Gen2 MPCs (MPC Live III, XL), installed by the Open MPC Plugin Manager.

Install it one way only. Ideas, bugs and criticism are all welcome: [open an issue](https://github.com/PotentialBreakfast/mpc-vst-potentialnoise/issues/new/choose).
